answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity atlas: every agent publishes a hashed commitment to its key in one epoch and may only reveal and start earning several epochs later. Like timber that must season before it bears load, a fresh identity carries no weight, so an attacker who mints a thousand keys through a single inlet pays a bond and a waiting cost on each one before any can vote or grade. Keys that reveal together and act in lockstep show up in the atlas, and their bonds are slashed.
